note: Ready-made setups for the start screen. A preset only picks a game, a balance package and rule switches that already exist; it adds no rules. Standard stays the engine default. All invention. Chosen by the assumptions council, 2026-11-23 (docs/council/2026-11-23-assumptions-council.md). The second island test (2026-11-26) is the island game with the rules Jacob made core after his first test; the first stays so its saves replay.

presets.name: Second island test
presets.summary: The island game with the rules Jacob made core after his first test (2026-11-26), and the contested board (thread 37): the offices are seats people fight over, each holder uses his seat every season, the assembly votes on seats each spring, losing a seat is a crisis, a few people climb a ladder of standing, and matters come from what just happened. Also: men who are refused come back with demands, grudges are never wiped, a rival needs a second faction behind him, quarrels are fought in the assembly, secrets are leverage, the purse runs dry when you squeeze a faction that already hates you, you choose who leads the army, and losing Syracuse sends you into exile instead of ending the game. After the second test: the guard dies only in battle, love holds a rival back, Carthage holds the towns it takes and spares Libya, the mint is an order, and petitions come with an offer. Thirty seasons, long enough to reach Carthage's war. The game checks in at seasons 10 and 20 and asks for your verdict at 30.

aim.text: Your first aim: build the citadel on the Island. With it you hold the three pillars of a tyranny (the citadel, the generalship and the treasury).

watch: Did thirty seasons give you a story you would tell someone? Which moment, and which person?
Did a few people come to matter more than the rest? Who?
When you lost something (an office, a city, a friend), did you notice at once?
Did Carthage's war come, and did it feel like Carthage's choice?
Was any screen, word or number confusing? Note where.

presets.name: Near-war test
presets.summary: The second island test's rules, with the war focus on (a war with aims, a ledger of turning points, weariness on both sides, peace with terms), started in spring 398 BC instead of 405. You hold the citadel, the Epipolae wall is up, Catana, Leontini and Aetna are yours, Messana is a friend, and Carthage is weak with plague. Carthage's anger is close to war. Each town's three leading houses lean to you, to Carthage or to the town alone (towns that choose). Fourteen seasons, to the end of the decade.

opening.text: Seven years after the peace with Carthage, you hold the citadel on the Island, and the new wall runs along Epipolae. Aetna, Catana and Leontini are yours, and Messana is your friend. In Libya a plague is killing Carthage's people. Some Greeks in Syracuse are leaving for Carthage's towns, but if there were war, every town that pays Carthage tribute might come over to you.
opening.why: the game opens near the war of 398 (Diodorus 14.14 to 14.18, 14.41, 14.44 to 14.45)

watch: Did the war feel like a story with a shape: why it began, what each side wanted, the turning points, how it ended?
Could you tell from the war strip how the war was going and what peace would cost?
Did Carthage's landing come as a warning first, or as a surprise?
Did any town do something on its own that you did not expect?
Was any screen, word or number confusing? Note where.

presets.name: First island test
presets.summary: The island game, set up for your first test: plots ripen slowly and grow from what you do, warnings are real clues, a blow can wound instead of kill, the chronicle follows people, and a beaten army can break. At the end of season 10 the game asks what you thought, then you play on.
watch: Did ten seasons give you a story you would tell someone? Which moment?
When a plot came for you, could you see it coming, and from whom? Did any blow feel random?
Did the island map matter, or did you play only the court? Did a town change sides, and did you know why?
Did Carthage feel like a power with its own goals, or like a timer?
Was any screen, word or number confusing? Note where.
